title: sendletter vs PostGrid for Letters in Canada
description: An honest comparison of sendletter and PostGrid for sending letters in Canada: pricing, features, test mode and idempotency, and who should choose which.
answer: PostGrid is a print-and-mail platform with country-specific sites and a free starter tier. Its pricing page lists $1.059 for a US first-class letter in US dollars, and its plans page shows different tier details. sendletter sends only to Canadian addresses, with no platform fee and letters from as low as $1.69 CAD all in.

rows: Built for
Letters to Canadian addresses
Print and mail across several countries, with separate country sites

None, no minimum

A free tier (up to 500 mailings a month on its pricing page; its plans page says 1,000). Its plans page lists Business at $449 or $499 a month and Growth at $900 or $999, depending on the copy of the page

$2.48 on your first, as low as $1.69 at volume, CAD, postage included

$1.059 per black-and-white first-class letter on the pricing page (USA, USD, includes printing, processing and postage). Its plans page shows a different free tier at $0.75 a letter, with no class or currency stated

Yes, identical key within 24 hours returns the same response

blocks.p: PostGrid's pricing page and its plans page, both read on November 26, 2026, describe the free tier differently (500 mailings a month on one, 1,000 on the other) and show different per-letter prices, without saying which country or mail class the second one is for. The two pages also give different monthly prices for its paid plans. That is not unusual for a company mid-change, but it means you should get a quote in writing. Its pricing text shows USD and says to talk to sales for pricing in local currency.

PostGrid links to a separate Canadian site, postgrid.ca, which we did not read, and its public API guide lists Canadian letter sizes. We did not find PostGrid's Canadian per-letter price on the pages we read, so we cannot compare it to ours. If you are a Canadian business sending to Canada, ask both companies what a letter to a Canadian address costs, in Canadian dollars, with postage.

ul: You send letters within Canada and want a flat, published price in Canadian dollars.
You want automatic volume pricing, a bulk endpoint, and a rate limit you will not hit by batching.
You want to be able to cancel a queued letter and see it on an invoice in your account.
You mail to several countries, or mostly outside Canada.
You need address verification or batch cleansing from the same vendor.
You need more mail types than a letter, or an enterprise plan.
